title: Backend engineering and system design core
goal: Design and build services that scale: APIs, caching, load balancing, replication, sharding, queues and rate limiting, and be able to justify each choice with numbers and trade-offs.

steps.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Martin Kleppmann)
steps.note: Read chapters 1 to 9 alongside the lessons. It is the best single book on this subject.

steps.title: The System Design Primer
steps.note: Free reference with diagrams and practice questions.

steps.title: The Twelve-Factor App
steps.note: Short and practical rules for deployable services.

steps.title: Design, build and load-test a URL shortener
steps.brief: Write a one-page design doc first (requirements, estimates, API, data model, trade-offs). Build it with a database, a cache and rate limiting, deploy it, and load test it with a tool such as k6 or wrk. Record the p50 and p99 latency before and after the cache.
steps.deliverable: A deployed service, a design doc in the repository and a results table showing how the cache changed latency and throughput.

steps.title: Case studies: chat, feed, video, maps, payments, and low-level design
steps.note: SD modules 17 to 28 are not written on this site yet. Practise them with the System Design Primer and DDIA examples, and sketch your own designs on paper first.

exit: You can run the full framework (clarify, estimate, API, data model, high-level design, deep dive, bottlenecks) on an unfamiliar problem in 45 minutes.
You can state at least two alternatives for every component you choose and why you rejected them.
Your deployed project has a design doc and measured numbers, not just a working demo.
